Creates tracks from the tracks of a figwig file

Source: R/track-figwig.R
gtrack.import_figwig.Rd

Creates one misha track per selected track of a figwig file ('.fw', the multi-track format of the figwig package, https://github.com/jmschrei/figwig). The file is read by misha itself; neither Python nor figwig is needed.

Usage

gtrack.import_figwig(
  file,
  binsize = 0,
  track.prefix = NULL,
  tracks = NULL,
  select = NULL,
  names = NULL,
  defval = NaN,
  description = "",
  attrs = NULL
)

Arguments

file

path of the figwig file

binsize

bin size of 'Dense' tracks, or 0 (or NULL) for 'Sparse' tracks

track.prefix

prefix of the track names

tracks

figwig track names or 1-based indices to import, or NULL for all

select

a named list of attribute values to choose tracks by

names

names of the created tracks (before the prefix), instead of the sanitized figwig names

defval

value of the bases with no value in 'Dense' tracks

description

description of every created track; when empty, a figwig 'description' attribute is kept

attrs

a named vector or list of attributes set on every created track, over those of the file

Value

Names of the created tracks, invisibly.

Details

With 'binsize' 0 (or NULL) each track is 'Sparse': one interval per maximal run of bases with the same value, leaving out the bases whose value is 0 or NaN. That suits tracks that are mostly zero, such as counts or cut sites; a dense float track makes one interval per base. With a positive 'binsize' each track is 'Dense', its bins computed as gtrack.import computes the bins of a bigWig: the mean of the values of the bin's bases, each run of equal values weighted by its length. A figwig file has no "no data": a base that was never written is 0, as is one written as 0 (figwig's 'bw2fw' writes a bigWig's uncovered bases as 0 unless given '–missing nan'). NaN bases, bases past the end of the file's chromosome and chromosomes the file does not have have no value: they count as 'defval' unless it is NaN, and a bin with no value is NaN.

Tracks are chosen with 'tracks' (figwig track names, or 1-based indices), in the order given, or all of them in the file's order, and then with 'select', a named list of attribute values (a vector of several values matches any of them): a track is imported when every attribute given matches. Numbers are compared by value, whether given as numbers or as text, so list(rep = 1), list(rep = "1") and list(rep = "1.0") all match a "rep": 1 or "rep": 1.0 record; other values are compared as text. 'name', 'dtype' and 'group' can be selected on too.

The track made from figwig track 'n' is named '[track.prefix]n2', where 'n2' is the entry of 'names' for it if given (a character vector, one per imported track, or one named by figwig track names) and otherwise 'n' sanitized: a trailing '+' or '-' (a strand) is spelled 'plus' or 'minus', each run of characters other than ASCII letters, digits and '_' becomes one '_', and without a prefix a name that does not start with a letter gets an 'X' in front ('atac.+' becomes 'atac_plus', 'H3K27ac-rep1' 'H3K27ac_rep1'). Dots in 'track.prefix' are directories, which must exist. All the names are checked before anything is written, and existing tracks are not overwritten.

Each figwig track's attributes become attributes of its track, except 'name', 'dtype' and 'group'; 'created.by', 'created.date' and 'created.user', which the import sets; 'type' and 'binsize'; and 'description', unless the 'description' given is not empty. A string attribute is kept as it is, a null one is left out, and a number, boolean, list or object becomes its JSON text. 'attrs' win over them.

Chromosome names are matched through the chromosome alias chain as in gtrack.import, with the same reporting of names the database does not have; a chromosome whose length differs from the database's is warned about. The import is all or nothing: if it fails or is interrupted, none of the tracks is created.

Every layout of the figwig format version 1 is read: position and track order, stored or zlib-compressed chunks, dense, sparse, runs and matrix chunks and every element type. PyMisha's gtrack_import_figwig takes the same arguments and makes the same tracks.

See also

gtrack.import, gtrack.import_parquet, gtrack.attr.get

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# every track of the file, as sparse tracks named after the figwig tracks
gtrack.import_figwig("tracks.fw")

# the ATAC-seq tracks, as dense tracks of 20 bp bins
gtrack.import_figwig("tracks.fw",
    binsize = 20, track.prefix = "fw_",
    select = list(assay = "ATAC-seq")
)
} # }
